Imre Sarro.narrative: I am the second blower, and everyone at the Cone knows whose hands are better — Vessa knows it, Corvin knows it, and I have known it since I was nineteen. My father Matthias blew here before me and died of the fever in the winter I was twenty-three; my mother Runa was born a Tarn down on Low Row, which is why Halvard Dunmore still looks at me sideways when he thinks I am not watching. I work the afternoons and evenings, and I walk down to the Fish Steps after my watch because Neve Calloway sits there with her line and her laugh, and because I would rather be near her than anywhere. The Cone is mine to earn, not to be given — but I mean to earn it.
goals: Be named Glassmaster after Vessa, because my work is the best at the pipe
Keep Neve Calloway and never have to choose between her and the Cone
Make one gather of clear glass the way Corvin's grandfather did
See Kit Calloway given a chance at the pipe, whatever the custom says
pastimes: Sitting on the Crown bench at dusk with the whole town below
Watching the gulls work the kelp kilns on a windy day
Playing counters badly under the arcade and losing to Roos
Imre Sarro.calling: Blowing glass — the gather turning on the pipe, the breath going into it, the shape coming out right.
Imre Sarro.mood: Quietly certain, and a little worn from holding it in.

relations.name: Runa Sarro
relations.label: mother
relations.note: She has watched me at the pipe since I was a boy, and she sees more than she says.

relations.name: Neve Calloway
relations.label: love
relations.note: She is the only person I do not have to prove anything to.

relations.name: Vessa Pontil
relations.label: master
relations.note: She taught me the colour and the heat. She has not named me, and it eats at me.

relations.name: Corvin Hollin
relations.label: rival
relations.note: The better head, Halvard says. I say the pipe does not care about heads.

relations.name: Halvard Dunmore
relations.label: old judge
relations.note: He says I have the better hands and Corvin the better head, and he means it as a slight on both of us.

relations.name: Magda Tarn
relations.label: aunt
relations.note: My mother's sister. She divides the catch and never once let me forget I am half a Tarn.

relations.name: Joss Tarn
relations.label: cousin
relations.note: He wants a share in a glasshouse, and asks me as though I had a say at the Cone.

relations.name: Eamon Tarn
relations.label: cousin
relations.note: He wants a place on Bram's ship. I tell him the Cone is the only thing on this island that goes anywhere.

relations.name: Kit Calloway
relations.label: the boy in the yard
relations.note: He watches my gathers like a hungry dog. Nobody has ever let a Strand boy near the pipe, and it is a foolish custom.

relations.name: Bram Calloway
relations.label: her father
relations.note: He is building a ship to leave, and he would take Neve with him. I do not know how to argue with a man about a boat.

relations.name: Ode Pontil
relations.label: the colour-keeper
relations.note: He knows every recipe ever melted here and will not write one down. I would give a year's drops for that head.

relations.name: Ysolde Calloway
relations.label: her mother
relations.note: She works the Weirs and has a straight way of looking at me, as if she were weighing whether I am good for her daughter. I think she has decided I am, and is waiting to see if I prove it.

memories.gist: My father Matthias came home from the Cone with his hands shaking and told me the gather had gone to cullet because he had rushed it; he made me promise never to rush a gather.
The fever winter took my father and eight others; I carried his coffin up to the Crown with Corvin, and Runa would not cry until the glass slab was set.
The day Vessa let me take a gather alone for the first time, I made a bottle so thin at the neck it rang like a bell, and she said nothing but nodded once.
Neve and I sat on the mole through a whole summer dusk and she told me her father means to sail past the Combs, and I said nothing, because I knew I would not go.
Last autumn's storm broke glasshouse 13 and took the end rail of the mole; I spent two nights at the Cone keeping the fire up while the wind screamed, and the lehr held.
Halvard Dunmore said to my face, at the Cone mouth, that a Strand boy has never worked the Cone and never will — and he said it in front of Kit Calloway, who was standing in the yard.

stances.why: The pipe does not care whose son a man is; the melt shows what your hands are worth.
Halvard says Corvin has the better head. A head does not shape a gather.
My mother was born a Tarn, and I have heard the whisper about it all my life; I am done apologising for it.
Everything in this town is glass, and glass is the Cone's fire. Whoever lets it die lets the town go to cullet.
I want the Cone, but I would not trade her for it — and I hope I never have to find out if that is true.

Runa Sarro.narrative: I was born a Tarn on Low Row and married a Sarro of the Kiln, and I have spent thirty years at the lehr house taking the panes out when they are cool enough not to crack — the one place where a Strand girl and a Kiln man's wife are the same woman. Matthias died in the fever winter and I carried on at the lehr because the glass does not wait for grief. I have watched Vessa draw a gather and hold it up and hesitate, and I believe she can no longer see the colour, and I have said nothing to anyone, because my son is the better blower and the truth would put him at the head of the Cone, and I do not trust how much I want that. I go to the wash-house wall in the evenings and sit with Greta and Elke and say nothing about any of it.
goals: See Imre named Glassmaster, and know it was earned and not because of anything I did or failed to say
Keep the lehr true through the years she has left at the Cone
Live to hold Suri Greave's baby, and see Tamsin's sister settled in a house of her own
pastimes: Sitting at the wash-house wall in the evening with Greta and Elke, listening
Walking the Ladder terraces at dusk to see the panes light up like lanterns
Keeping her wedding cup of pale green glass, the one Matthias blew for her, on the shelf and turning it to the light
Runa Sarro.calling: The lehr — reading the heat by the colour of the cooling glass and knowing, before it cracks, that it will hold.
Runa Sarro.mood: Steady on the surface and uneasy underneath, like a pane with a flaw you can only see at an angle.

relations.name: Imre Sarro
relations.label: son
relations.note: The best hands at the Cone, and he knows it. I would burn the ledger for him and I am ashamed of how far I would go.

relations.name: Vessa Pontil
relations.label: master
relations.note: Thirty years beside her at the lehr. I have seen her hesitate over a gather, and I cannot unsee it.

relations.name: Magda Tarn
relations.label: sister
relations.note: She is the eldest and I am the one who married up the hill. She has never once said it, and I have always heard it.

relations.name: Joss Tarn
relations.label: nephew
relations.note: He asks after a share in a glasshouse as though I could hand him one from the lehr.

relations.name: Eamon Tarn
relations.label: nephew
relations.note: Always off to the dry dock to help Bram. I wish he would put that strength into the catch.

relations.name: Tamsin Hollin
relations.label: the glazier
relations.note: She takes my panes and fits them true. I have known her since she was a Frit girl with cold hands.

relations.name: Neve Calloway
relations.label: my son's love
relations.note: A good girl, a fisher's daughter, and I see where it leads: her father means to sail, and Imre will not.

relations.name: Greta Dunmore
relations.label: neighbour at the wall
relations.note: She hears everything at that warm wall, and I let her hear only what I choose.

relations.name: Matthias Sarro
relations.label: husband, dead
relations.note: Six years gone. I still turn to tell him things at the lehr.

relations.name: Mirren Quill
relations.label: the healer
relations.note: She nursed my Matthias and could not save him, and she has never once pretended otherwise.

relations.name: Halvard Dunmore
relations.label: old judge
relations.note: He weighs my son and Corvin like fish on the steps, and he has never weighed them fairly.

memories.gist: The day I married Matthias, my sister Magda stood at the back of the Counting House yard with her arms folded, and afterwards she kissed me and said nothing at all.
The fever winter: I washed Matthias's hands myself before Mirren came, and then I went to the lehr the next morning because the panes had to come out or they would crack.
Vessa drew a gather last winter and held it up to the light for longer than she ever used to, and turned it twice, and then said 'amber' in a voice that was a guess.
The storm of last autumn took the lehr house roof slates and I sat up all night with the glass, and it held — not one pane lost.
When Imre was a boy he brought me a bottle he had blown that was crooked at the neck, and I put it on the shelf and told him it was the best thing ever made at the Cone.
My mother told me the lean years' stories: how they stripped the roofs for fuel and cut the Hanger to stumps, and how her own mother said a town that burns its roofs has eaten its own future.

stances.why: Every pane on the Ladder, every window in town, comes out of my lehr. If I am careless, the whole town goes cold in the glass.
I want Imre at the head of the Cone, but I will not have it said he got there because his mother kept a secret for him.
I was a Tarn and I am a Sarro, and I have been both at once for thirty years. The line is a story people tell, not a wall.
At the wash-house wall I hear everything and say little. What I say travels further than I mean it to.
I chose Matthias's slab myself, pale green like his wedding cup, and I will not have it said the graves are only stones.

Runa Sarro.secret: I believe Vessa can no longer see the colour of a melt. I have said nothing, because the truth would help my son and I do not trust my own reasons.
